$comment: English texts of data/guilds.json (src/engine/overlay.js): the Guild's tabs, the Guild Hall (Siedziba) with its buildings, the Guild Expedition, the Guild Beast, the Guild Trials, the Guild Requests, the Resource exchange, the Guild Chest, the guild wars (War: the teams, Team I–VI, the battles, the war chest; the test version's Mirror Guild) and the guilds' Fame in the Ranking. A Hall building's `accusative` is its plain name; the sentences put "the" before it ("Donate to the Banner?"). The forms after a number (attackForms, trialForms, counted, pieceForms…) are [one, other, other] for the Polish [one, few, many]. Guild roles: lider leader, zastępca deputy. The Exchange's button „Wymień” is “Exchange”.

texts.title: Guild Hall
texts.intro: The Hall's buildings give bonuses to every guild member. You donate gold and resources to the building you choose yourself.
how: The guild has no common purse. Each member donates their own gold and resources to the building they choose. Donations are not returned, even after leaving the guild.

Each building grows from zero to level {max}. It reaches the next level when the donations to it cover the whole cost of that level: the gold and the resource. Whatever you donate beyond the cost carries over to the next level.
The first level costs {firstGold} gold and {firstResource} of the resource, and each one after it costs more, up to {lastGold} gold and {lastResource} of the resource at level {max}.
The leader and deputies can mark buildings as preferred, so the guild knows what to save up for now. It is only a hint: you donate to whatever you like.
The bonuses work for every guild member. An exploration takes them from the moment it sets out, and the Anvil from the moment of upgrading. After leaving the guild, the bonuses are gone.

texts.title: Guild Expedition
texts.lead: The members' exploration minutes lead the guild through {stages} stages. At the end of each stage a guardian bars the way.
how: Every week, from Monday at midnight, the guild sets out on a new route through the land at the members' average level.
Every minute of a guild member's exploration moves the route on once they claim the report. Quick Hunts and Party explorations count too.
A stage is {perMember} minutes of exploration for each active guild member.
A guardian waits at the end of a stage. The route stands still until the guild defeats it. Minutes gathered in the meantime wait and move the route on right after it falls.
Everyone who added minutes this week attacks the guardian: {attacks} times a day, separately from the attacks on the Beast. An attack is one fight with full HP and no potions.
Each next guardian is stronger. A defeated one gives a chest to everyone who added minutes this week. The last one also gives rare loot: an item of your class.
A defeated guardian also gives the guild Fame in the Ranking: {fame} for each one, and {fameLast} for the last.
You can claim the chest until the end of next week.

texts.title: Guild Beast
texts.lead: Every week the whole guild hunts one beast. The damage stays on its shared HP bar.
rules: The beast is the champion of one of the lands, at the guild members' average level. The more members, the more HP it has.
Each character attacks {attacks} times a day, separately from the entries to the Towers. New attacks come at midnight.
An attack is one fight with full HP and no potions, with the result at once. It gives no XP, gold or loot. You can attack during an exploration, too.
The beast stays until Sunday midnight. On Monday a new one comes.
Every character that attacks the beast at least once gets a Beast Chest. If the beast falls, the chest holds an item of the character's class at their level and the beast's materials.
If the beast survives the week, the chest holds only materials: the more of the bar the guild took off, the more of them (from 25, 50 and 75%). Below 25% there is no chest.
You can open the chest from the beast's fall or from the end of the week, until the end of the next week at the latest.

texts.title: Guild Trials
texts.intro: Every day more trials from all over the game appear on the board. They all count at once: you complete them in ordinary play, and the guild draws closer to the chests.
how: Trials need not be taken: all of those on the board count at once. What you do in ordinary play advances every matching trial from the moment it appears on the board, and its numbers suit your character's level.

On Monday the board has {first} trials, and every day {daily} new ones are added. At most {perDay} of your trials go onto the guild's bar for each day of the week: {twoDays} in all by Tuesday, {threeDays} by Wednesday, and so on. Those completed beyond that will go onto the bar on the following days.
The members' completed trials fill a shared bar with {thresholds} thresholds. Each threshold reached gives a chest to everyone who completes at least one trial this week.

The thresholds grow with the number of active members, that is, those whose account was in the game in the last {days} days, counted when the board is drawn. Whoever joins later raises the thresholds in part: the fewer days left until Sunday, the less.
The chest holds gold, Time Points and the material of creatures from the place your class goes to. The last four thresholds also give System Points.
You can claim the chest until the end of next week. A new board comes on Monday at midnight.

texts.title: Guild Requests
texts.intro: Short of a material, herb, potion or mineral? Ask the guild, and others will give from their stores.
how: You can have one request up at a time, for up to {most} of one material, herb, potion or mineral. You can add the next one {wait} hours after the previous. You can withdraw a request no one has given anything to yet and add a new one at once.
A request stays up until someone fills it, until you withdraw it, or for {open} hours. The pieces given come to you at once, with the giver's name, and you thank each gift with a single tap.

Herbs and potions go to the bag, so they need room in it. You cannot ask for items or gold. The Encyclopedia will not count the pieces given: only what the character obtains or makes on their own counts.
Giving brings no gold or System rewards. It counts towards the Benefactors of the week ranking and the Guild Trials. Characters of one account do not give each other anything.

texts.title: Resource exchange
texts.intro: Too much stone and too little wood? Post an offer, and someone in the guild will take it. You can also sell and buy resources for gold.
how: An offer is pieces of one resource for pieces of another, or a resource for gold and gold for a resource: from 1 to {most} pieces of a resource and from 1 to {goldMost} gold. {counts}
The pieces you give leave your resources or your gold at once and wait in the offer.
An offer is taken whole. Whoever taps “Exchange” gives what you want and gets what you give. Your part comes to you at once.
You can post at most {offers} at a time. Each stays up for at most {open}, and you can withdraw it at any moment.
The pieces of an offer come back to you whole when you withdraw it, when its time runs out, or when you leave the guild.
Characters of one account do not exchange with each other.

texts.title: Guild Chest
texts.intro: Leave an item in the chest, and someone from the guild takes it when they look in. You do not have to play at the same time.
how: Put an item from your bag in for everyone or for one character of the guild. A worn item cannot go in.
An item for everyone can be taken by any guild member. An item for one character can be taken only by them, and while it waits, you can take it back.
The chest holds {capacity}. To take an item, you need room in your bag.
Items go in and come out from character level {level}, as in the Exchange. You can take your own item back before that too.
An item keeps its upgrade, gem, rarity and Tier. The Encyclopedia does not count an item from another character.
“Recent moves” show up to {log}: who puts in or takes out what, and when.
When someone leaves the guild, the items for them are for everyone from then on. The last character can leave the guild only once the chest is empty.

how: Every week, from Monday to Sunday, the guild fights another guild with a similar number of members. The game draws the rival on Monday at midnight. Guilds in which characters of the same account play are never drawn against each other.

Members form teams of {size}: the guild has as many teams as it has full fives of members, at most {max}, and a guild of fewer than {size} people has one. You take a place in a team yourself, and the leader and deputies can move anyone.
Members without a team are in the reserve: before a battle they take the free places in the teams. A team still short of people fights short-handed, e.g. 3 against 5.

Every day at {hour} the teams fight 5 on 5 battles. Characters fight as they are saved, as in the Arena, without companions or mercenaries. The team with someone still standing wins. You can watch every battle afterwards.

There are as many battles as the bigger of the two guilds has teams. The smaller guild's teams fight in turn, several times: 2 teams against the rival's 4 teams make 4 battles, and each of the two teams fights twice.

The guild that wins more battles by Sunday wins the war. For winning the war the guild collects {fame} and a war chest for the Guild Chest: an item of a champion's rarity for each of its teams. In a draw nobody collects them.
For every battle won in which you fight, you collect {gold} gold and {systemPoints}. The gold grows with the character's level.
limitWin: After {moves} moves the judge ends the battle: the team with more HP left wins.
limitDraw: After {moves} moves the judge ends the battle: both teams have almost the same HP left, so it is a draw.

texts.lead: Fame is the guild's points for what its members do together. The week starts on Monday at midnight.
how: Guild Beast: {beastPercent} for each full 1% of the week's beast bar, and {beastFell} for its fall.
Guild Expedition: {perGuardian} for each guardian defeated, and {lastGuardian} for the seventh, the last.
Guild Trials: {perTrial} for each trial completed. At most {trialCap} trials count from one character, as on the Trials bar.
Guild Requests: {perPiece} for each piece given to a guild member. At most {giftCap} pieces count from one character.
Exchange: {perExchange} for each exchange. At most {exchangeCap} exchanges count from one character that takes offers.
“All time” is the Fame of all the weeks, this one included.
The guild with the most Fame in the previous week has a gold tag for the whole week. In a tie, the older guild wins.
